core_summary: Heat energy flows spontaneously from regions of higher temperature to regions of lower temperature via three mechanisms: Conduction (particle vibration in solids without net particle displacement), Convection (bulk fluid movement in liquids and gases driven by density differences), and Radiation (electromagnetic thermal waves requiring no medium). Thermal conduction varies across conductors and insulators. Convection currents drive atmospheric weather, including Land Breeze and Sea Breeze in coastal areas.
key_concepts: To visualize fluid convection currents using a potassium permanganate (KMnO4) crystal in water.

key_terms.definition: Heat transfer in liquids and gases caused by physical movement of fluid due to temperature and density gradients.
A cool wind blowing from the sea toward the land during daytime.

key_takeaways: Sea breeze blows during DAYTIME (sea -> land). Land breeze blows at NIGHTTIME (land -> sea).
